source_snapshot.items: Check KVM sessions status after refresh
source_snapshot.procedure: Login BMC Web, use product Refresh, login/use browser F5, then check whether user remains logged in.
source_snapshot.criteria: User remains logged in after F5.
source_snapshot.script: No Master command; 5 attended/5 machine minutes; unique row/code/variant.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; tests Web login persistence but does not observe the title's KVM session.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/MEDIUM; records title/body Source Conflict and separates Web authentication from KVM connection continuity.

old_problem: The title requires KVM session status, while Procedure/Criteria check only the BMC Web authentication session. These are distinct cookie/websocket/client layers, so either one alone would drop coverage.
disposition_reason: ED-19/20 prohibit deleting either title or body coverage. Both can be retained as independent subtests under the same row: A validates BMC Web authentication through product Refresh and browser F5; B keeps one mapped benign KVM session open and validates its connection/video continuity across the same actions. Exact browser/KVM/session semantics remain runtime project configuration.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2237, same-row DeepSeek columns, GPT V2, historical record, unique identity and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next formal row Functionality 2238 / Wistron-BMC Sanity-00020-V001 / 3340759d9eb37176 was directly read from XLSX and its historical record.
Use one dedicated test account, verified BMC/SUT/role and separate recovery administrator; record non-secret Web and KVM session identifiers.
Subtest A: from a safe non-state-changing page, perform the product Refresh once and browser F5 once, proving the same target/role remains authenticated after each.
Subtest B: launch one benign mapped KVM console before those actions and separately prove connection status plus fresh video/target continuity after each operation.
Web login cannot prove KVM survival; a surviving KVM websocket cannot prove the main Web session remains authenticated.
Ensure no form resubmission, wrong-target navigation, duplicate KVM session, console input or secret cookie/token capture.
Stop on logout, CSRF/error, KVM disconnect/stale wrong-host video, duplicate session or access fault; no blind credential retry.
No login, Refresh/F5, KVM launch/input, cleanup, retry or DUT action was executed.

test_case.test_name: Separate BMC Web authentication and KVM continuity across Refresh and F5
test_case.purpose: Validate independently that the BMC Web login and one active correctly mapped KVM console session each persist safely across the product Refresh action and browser F5.
required_package: BMC/SUT/WebUI, supported browser and KVM client/version
Dedicated account/role, concurrency/timeout/CSRF semantics and recovery administrator
Exact product Refresh versus F5 sequence and non-secret Web persistence oracle
KVM connection/video freshness/target oracle and final session cleanup policy
test_case.test_command: Run two correlated checkpoints with the same verified target/account: A records Web authentication, performs product Refresh once and F5 once, and checks same-target/role authentication after each; B starts one benign mapped KVM session, repeats the actions, and separately records connection plus fresh correct-target video continuity. Do not resubmit forms, expose tokens, create duplicate sessions or send console input.
test_case.expected_result: After each named refresh action, the Web session remains authenticated to the same BMC/role and the pre-existing KVM session remains connected with fresh correct-target video; no form resubmission, duplicate session, secret exposure or unexpected logout occurs.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires complete independent A-Web and B-KVM evidence. Web persistence cannot pass KVM and KVM persistence cannot pass Web. Logout, wrong target/role, CSRF error, form resubmission, duplicate session, KVM disconnect or stale/wrong-host video is FAIL. Missing runtime bindings blocks execution, not review.
safety_gate: Gate CLOSED until target/account, safe page, refresh sequence, KVM oracle, concurrency/final state and recovery are signed.
Never capture cookies/tokens/passwords or sensitive console content.
No state-changing form, KVM input, virtual media, power control or credential retry.
Stop on target/session/access anomaly and preserve non-secret evidence.
expected_evidence: Approved Refresh/F5 sequence and safe-page proof
Per-step KVM connection plus fresh correct-target video evidence
BMC session/audit timestamps, no-resubmission/no-duplicate/no-secret audit and cleanup/final state
test_case.recovery: On logout or KVM/access anomaly, do not retry credentials or refresh repeatedly. Preserve session/audit evidence, close only under the signed cleanup plan, and use the independent recovery account to restore the approved final session state.

source_conflict.reason: Title KVM scope and body Web-login scope are preserved as separate required subtests with independent oracles; neither substitutes for the other.

blocked.reason: Both session layers and refresh operations are clear; browser/KVM semantics are parameterizable.
